briefings.title: 2026 Annual Meetings Curtain Raiser: Outlook for the Global Economy and Policy Priorities
briefings.tldr: The global economy faces a complex clash between a positive AI demand shock and negative supply shocks from high energy costs and record public debt, requiring urgent structural reforms and fiscal consolidation.

briefings.title: IMF MD on the Global Economic Outlook
briefings.tldr: Global economic growth is proving resilient at around 3%, supported by positive AI demand and emerging market strength, but faces persistent risks from sticky inflation, rising debt-servicing costs, and AI-driven financial stability concerns.

briefings.title: IMF Chief Praises Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole Speech
briefings.tldr: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva praised Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech for its clarity on price stability, while warning that high global debt levels and rapid technological innovation complicate central bank efforts to manage inflation.

briefings.title: Press Briefing: 2026 Euro Area Consultations
briefings.tldr: The IMF has revised the Euro Area's economic outlook downward—projecting 0.9% growth in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027—due to persistent energy shocks and geopolitical tensions.

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: IMF’s Georgieva press briefing at Spring Meetings
briefings.tldr: The global economy faces a precarious slowdown driven by "shock upon shock," with global public debt on track to hit 100% of GDP by 2029 and energy supply disruptions from the Middle East threatening to deepen inflationary pressures and suppress growth to as low as 2%.

briefings.title: IMF Chief To Unveil Global Policy Agenda Live
briefings.tldr: The global economy faces a "shock upon shock" scenario driven by conflict in the Middle East, with growth projections slowing to 3.1% (and potentially 2% in adverse cases) as public debt is on track to reach post-WWII levels by 2029.

briefings.title: Full Interview: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva
briefings.tldr: The global economy faces a significant "asymmetric shock" driven by Middle East conflict and AI disruption, yet remains surprisingly resilient due to private sector agility and technological innovation.

briefings.title: LIVE: IMF Chief Georgieva Delivers Curtain-Raiser Speech Before Spring Meet | N18G
briefings.tldr: The global economy is facing a severe supply shock driven by conflict in the Middle East, necessitating a downgrade in growth projections due to energy disruptions, infrastructure damage, and rising inflation.

briefings.title: LIVE: IMF Managing Director speaks ahead of the IMF/World Bank spring meetings
briefings.tldr: The global economy faces a severe, asymmetric supply shock driven by Middle East conflict, resulting in significant energy disruptions, slowed growth, and heightened food insecurity.

briefings.title: Asia in 2050 Roundtable: Challenges Ahead for Central Banks in Asia
briefings.tldr: To sustain growth through 2050, Asian economies must pivot from export-led manufacturing toward regional integration, service-oriented sectors, and digital innovation while institutionalizing macroeconomic stability to survive a "new normal" of constant global shocks.

briefings.title: Exclusive: Kristalina Georgieva, MD, IMF On AI, Growth & India’s Global Rise
briefings.tldr: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva projects that AI could boost global growth by 0.8%, but warns of a "tsunami" hitting labor markets that requires India’s model of "democratized" digital infrastructure to prevent widening global inequality.

briefings.title: IMF Chief Kristalina Georgieva Exclusive Interview on India's AI Moment | World Exclusive Interview
briefings.tldr: AI represents a "tsunami" for the global labor market that could boost global growth by 0.8%, but its benefits must be democratized through digital public infrastructure and robust social safety nets to prevent a widening gap between "haves" and "have-nots."

briefings.title: The questions top Davos leaders are asking to start 2026
briefings.tldr: As the global order shifts toward a permanent state of multipolar uncertainty, leaders in 2026 must abandon nostalgia for past stability in favor of "thinking the unthinkable," prioritizing structural independence, and distinguishing between mere organizational momentum and meaningful impact.

briefings.title: IMF's Georgieva on the Growing Influence of EM, Decline of US Dollar
briefings.tldr: Emerging markets now drive 75% of global growth and 56% of global GDP, yet they face a "fog of uncertainty" that requires rebuilding depleted fiscal buffers and navigating geopolitical volatility.

briefings.title: Davos 2026 IMFs Kristalina Georgieva on whats next for AI skills and the global economy
briefings.tldr: The global economy shows surprising resilience with upgraded growth projections despite pervasive uncertainty, driven by private sector dynamism and muted trade tensions.
